video.title: STATS OVERLOAD: The Craziest Fantasy Basketball Draft

summary: Josh Lloyd and Dan Besbris do a joke two-team, 50-round roto draft with 94 categories, no bench and no moves all season. They use the picks to talk about real player values for normal 9-cat drafts. Main takes: Tyrese Maxey and Lauri Markkanen are being priced inconsistently, the Atlanta backcourt (Nickeil Alexander-Walker, Dyson Daniels, CJ McCollum) is undervalued, and Matas Buzelis, Franz Wagner and Paul George are safe values. Josh's main principle is that finding value beats every other strategy. When no pick has clear upside, he takes a player he is confident will hold his draft spot. They are cautious on injured players like Coby White, on rookies, and on unclear roles like Ryan Rollins and Jaden McDaniels.

rules.text: Josh: the first round tends to bunch together behind injury-prone guys who are high per game. If you can guess which player will play 72 or more games, you probably win that pick.
rules.quote: if you can guess which one's going to play 72 games or more, you probably somehow win that pick

rules.text: Josh says the number one way to win fantasy is getting value, in the draft and off the waiver wire. Finding a top 40 player at 100 beats any build or pairing.
rules.quote: If you find a top 40 player at 100, it trumps everything else.

rules.text: Josh first looks for a player who can beat his draft slot. If no one around that pick can, he takes a player he is confident will not fall below where he is drafted.
rules.quote: do I feel confident this guy's going to be this good, >> but also probably not slip behind it

rules.text: Josh does not like drafting a player only because a teammate might get hurt. He says it does give some upside, though.
rules.quote: I don't like to take people just thinking that maybe someone gets hurt but at least it does give you some sort of upside

rules.text: Dan: early-season hot streaks from players like Dennis Schroder do not hold up. Draft them only for the first few games.
rules.quote: If you if you're drafting for any reason other than like the first four games of the year, you're doing it wrong.

rules.text: Dan says guards are going cheaper this season and big men cost more than usual.
rules.quote: I feel like guards are weirdly cheaper this season. Big men got more expensive for the first time

rules.text: Rookies are risky because they often need months to adjust. Dan avoids drafting them because he fears the unknown.
rules.quote: it's because I hate the unknown. I fear it.

rules.text: Dan says players get marked down because of a vague fear their team will tank. He does not share that fear.
rules.quote: Larry Markin is just getting dinged because of the the folks have this like latent tank fear thing

rules.text: Dan: in Yahoo public leagues, other managers take about 20 random players in the first 110 picks. That lets the solid mid-round players slip about 20 picks.
rules.quote: 20 random dudes that don't belong are going to get taken at some point in the first 110 picks

rules.text: Josh warns that players promised a starting role by a new team often lose it within a few games. Dan calls this Buddy Hield syndrome.
rules.quote: players get promised come sign with us and you'll start Jaylen Smith in Indiana and then he starts at power for

rules.text: Dan says he weighs turnovers more because he is a roto player. How he values a player can depend on the rest of the roster.
rules.quote: I'm I'm I'm know that I'm more of a roto guy, so I I care more about it than the average bear.

player_notes.text: Dan expects Maxey to drop off a little this season but still go around the end of the first or start of the second round. Josh does not see him as a first-round player this season.
player_notes.quote: he's going to have a little drop off this year, but I think he'll probably still be like end of first, beginning of second

player_notes.text: Josh doubts Maxey can repeat his high steals. New teammates could take his assists, shots and usage, and Nick Nurse might trim his minutes. Josh does not think he is a strong defender.
player_notes.quote: What if Nick Nurse says, "We're a bit stacked. Let's ease the minutes off by one." and then the steals go to 1.1

player_notes.text: Josh would rank Kevin Durant and Cooper Flagg ahead of Maxey, and Maxey ahead of Scottie Barnes and Jalen Johnson.
player_notes.quote: Actually, I'd have Durant and Flag both ahead of him. Um I would have him ahead of like Barnes.

player_notes.text: Josh says Maxey only drops about three spots even with Embiid, Jaylen Brown and LeBron James around him, and some people take him at pick six or seven.
player_notes.quote: he gets dinged three spots in some I've seen people taking him at pick six or or pick seven

player_notes.text: Asked about the Achilles injury, Dan is neutral on Tatum. He sees him as one of many first-round players bunched together.
player_notes.quote: Tatum and Ant and Donovan Mitchell and Maxi and Jaylen Johnson and the list goes on and on

player_notes.text: Of Donovan Mitchell, Jamal Murray and Austin Reaves, Dan picks Reaves as most likely to finish top 12. Josh says it is probably Murray and does not think it is Mitchell.
player_notes.quote: I think it's probably Reeves, but I I think >> that's who I'm going with here.

player_notes.text: Josh expects Reaves to have more turnovers and a worse FG% than Jamal Murray.
player_notes.quote: Reeves is going to get a lot a lot more turnovers, isn't he? He's And he's probably going to be a worse field goal

player_notes.text: Dan is not a big Bam Adebayo fan this year.
player_notes.quote: I'm going to take BAM out a bio. >> Yeah, that's okay. I'm not a huge BAM guy this year.

player_notes.text: Josh is not high on Chet Holmgren this season. He would not take him in the first two rounds.
player_notes.quote: I'm not a big Czech guy this season either. I I wouldn't take Ched in the first two rounds.

player_notes.text: Dan would not take Curry this early in a normal 9-cat draft. He expects Curry could miss 30 games.
player_notes.quote: I'm not doing this in a regular nine cap, but I'm going to go Steph.

player_notes.text: Josh took Embiid at pick 27 here for the per-game categories. In a real draft he took him at pick 61 and says he would not normally take him at 27.
player_notes.quote: I did take him in my JLFB bowl draft at 61 on my Jokic team.

player_notes.text: Josh says Markkanen was about 8th in per-game 9-cat rankings last season. He is now dropping 30 to 40 spots in drafts because of Jaren Jackson Jr. and the arrival of Darryn Peterson. Josh still says no one should take him in the first round.
player_notes.quote: he's getting dinged like 40 spots, 30 spots in a lot of drafts.

player_notes.text: Dan thinks Markkanen goes around pick 40 instead of in the 20s because of tank fear, which he does not share.
player_notes.quote: that's probably why he's going near 40 instead of >> 20s which is still a bigger ding than Maxi

player_notes.text: Sabonis is the best at assists plus rebounds combined.
player_notes.quote: Demonus Sabonis. He's king of the ass bound.

player_notes.text: Both hosts like Dejounte Murray this year, but his draft position keeps falling, now to around 70.
player_notes.quote: He's like down to like 70 or something at the moment.

player_notes.text: Josh thinks Trey Murphy has slid too far in drafts.
player_notes.quote: I think they both slid too far. I'm going to take Trey Murphy.

player_notes.text: Coby White is out for the preseason with another calf injury, the same thing as last season. Josh was taking him in the 60s and 70s but will now push him down to the 90s.
player_notes.quote: Kobe White is now out for preseason with another calf injury. This is Deja Vuan. the same thing last season.

player_notes.text: Miller is the last healthy main player left in Charlotte. That is part of why Josh took him.
player_notes.quote: he's the last man alive in Charlotte. >> That's what's I was just That's part of why I took him

player_notes.quote: Every year he's the same guy. It doesn't translate to fantasy.

player_notes.text: Dan thinks the 40s is a fine range for Jalen Williams.
player_notes.quote: I took Jaylen Williams. I feel like the 40s is fine for him.

player_notes.text: Josh thinks Alexander-Walker is going too low in the 60s and 70s. His free throw percentage jumped, his true shooting was about 70% over the final 30 games, and his role and minutes are unchanged.
player_notes.quote: and he had a true shooting of like 70% for the final 30 games which again is not going to happen

player_notes.text: Josh says McCollum is going for $1 in auctions and around pick 118. He thinks that is too low.
player_notes.quote: even C Mullen like I he's going $1 in auctions and I pick 118.

player_notes.text: Josh has avoided McCollum in fantasy because his free throw percentage is unreliable and his defensive stats are usually very poor.
player_notes.quote: he's been so unreliable with his uh free throw percentage. His defensive stats are usually putrid.

player_notes.text: Josh thinks Clingan is early around pick 50. He is a good rebounder and shot blocker but cannot finish, does not pass, and is terrible at free throws.
player_notes.quote: I'm not into a guy that is a centered also can't finish and has like not really particularly high field goal percentage. Doesn't pass.

player_notes.text: Josh says Clingan had knee and ankle problems in his first two years.
player_notes.quote: Well, it didn't cuz he had his knee and ankle problems the first two years.

player_notes.text: Josh calls Banchero a big assists-plus-rebounds player. Dan normally would not draft him.
player_notes.quote: I know that you normally wouldn't touch him, so I'm just going to take him here anyway

player_notes.text: Josh thinks Bane played all 82 games last year after playing about 40 the year before. He doubts Bane will repeat that.
player_notes.quote: didn't I think Bane played all 82 last year, right?

player_notes.quote: If he um if Nick Claxton hadn't pinged his hammy today, he might have been a big riser

player_notes.text: Josh says Buzelis rose from 80 on Yahoo to about 69 but has not risen enough. He played about 29 minutes a game last season, and Josh sees no playing-time worry.
player_notes.quote: he played like 29 minutes a game last season. I don't really think that's going to be too much of a problem

player_notes.text: Dan tries to get Buzelis in the 60s. Both expect him to finish around 50 in 9-cat.

player_notes.text: Both hosts like Paul George this season. Josh rejects the idea that he will be a low-usage role player for the Celtics. He was the Sixers' best player in many playoff games last season.
player_notes.quote: He was literally the six's best player in a lot of those playoff games for them last season.
